**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement contains no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binding Sparkling:

- **§ 2 (Grant)** — the licence is "non-transferable and non-exclusive," a limit on Garman's grant, not a restriction on our sourcing.
- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — ordinary licence-scope limits (no copying, reverse engineering, sublicensing, use outside authorisation); no requirements-purchase or "shall not procure from any third party" covenant.
- **§ 10 / § 11 (Maintenance and Fees)** — maintenance is a renewable one-year service commitment from Garman; it does not appoint Garman as our sole or exclusive provider.
- Other "exclusive" hits are the § 15 exclusive-remedy clause, the § 16 non-exclusive escrow licence, and non-exclusive jurisdiction in the governing-law provision — none is a restrictive covenant on us.

This sits at the playbook's preferred position (no exclusivity on Customer), so we keep full freedom to buy from other suppliers and no change is needed.
